audience: Marketers, PPC/email/social practitioners, and small business owners running their own campaign tracking

questions.question: What are the required UTM parameters for accurate tracking?
questions.answer_summary: Google recommends always using utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign together as the core set.

questions.question: Are UTM parameter values case-sensitive?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — 'utm_source=google' and 'utm_source=Google' are treated as different values, so lowercase is advised as a standard.

questions.question: Why does my traffic show as (not set) in the source/medium report?
questions.answer_summary: Missing UTM parameters on a link cause the visit to show as '(not set)' in reporting, reducing data quality.

questions.question: Why is my single campaign split into multiple rows in reports?
questions.answer_summary: Inconsistent capitalization or naming (e.g. 'SpringSale' vs 'Spring_Sale') is treated as distinct values, fragmenting the data.

questions.question: What is the utm_term parameter for?
questions.answer_summary: It's used to identify paid search keywords associated with an ad.

questions.question: What is the utm_content parameter for?
questions.answer_summary: It differentiates between creative variations (e.g. ad copy or images) within the same campaign.

questions.question: Does skipping UTM tagging break marketing attribution?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — attribution guidance flags missing UTM parameters as a root cause of unreliable attribution data.

questions.question: What free tool does Google provide for building UTM links?
questions.answer_summary: Google's Campaign URL Builder lets marketers add campaign parameters to URLs to measure custom campaigns in Google Analytics.
